title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from pp. 93-95). A 'disposition' E is a set E with a family Σ_E ⊂ P(E) of distinguished subsets. Σ_E is a complete lattice with an internal Sup. Each point x has a 'support' σ_E(x) ∈ Σ_E, its smallest distinguished set. For A ⊂ E, supp°_E(A) = Sup_{x∈A} σ_E(x). Every S ∈ Σ_E satisfies S = Sup_{x∈S} σ_E(x), so the σ_E(x) generate Σ_E under sups. A model to keep in mind is E a preorder and Σ_E its down-sets (an Alexandrov topology), with σ_E(x) the principal down-set of x. Since Σ_E carries its own Sup, it may be more general than a family closed under unions.

The page states a scholie with three equivalent descriptions of a morphism ('correspondence') E → E':
(1) Corr(Σ,Σ'): maps α_*: Σ_E → Σ_{E'} commuting with arbitrary Sups, hence monotone. These are morphisms in the category of sup-lattices.
(2) Corr(E,E'): maps α: E → Σ_{E'} ⊂ P(E') satisfying (a) α(x) ∈ Σ_{E'}, and (b) the equivalent conditions of 'C prop. 4', most explicitly (iv). From p. 95, (iv b) is a monotonicity/support compatibility: y ∈ σ_E(x) ⇒ α(y) ≤ α(x), and α̅(σ_E(x)) has the same support as α(x).
(3) Corr*(E,E'): set-theoretic relations R ⊂ E×E' such that R(x) ∈ Σ_{E'} for all x ∈ E and ^tR(x') ∈ Σ_E for all x' ∈ E'. These are relations whose fibres on both sides are distinguished sets.

The canonical bijections are:
- φ(α_*) = α_* ∘ σ_E, i.e. restrict a sup-map to the generators.
- The inverse of φ is α ↦ (S ↦ Sup_{x∈S} α(x)); this is proved on p. 95.
- ψ(α) = {(x,x') | x' 'disjoint from'/not in α(x)}. That is, the relation has fibres compl_{E'}(α(x)) obtained by composing with a complement-type operation c_{E'}. Grothendieck explicitly remarks that ψ(α) is not the graph of α but of c_{E'} ∘ α.

In the preorder model this is the standard fact that sup-maps between down-set lattices correspond to monotone maps E → Σ_{E'}. These in turn correspond to monotone relations (profunctors with values in 2), where the complement passage converts down-set-valued maps into relations whose transposed fibres are distinguished sets. This is the usual Galois-type duality between sup-maps and relations.

Purpose: to set up the category of dispositions. On p. 95, §11.7, morphisms are these correspondences, composed by β ∘_dis α = supp° (β ∘_ens α).
errors: The ψ construction requires that complements (or a complement-type operation c_{E'}) send fibres back into Σ_{E'}, or into Σ_E on the transposed side. For an arbitrary sup-closed Σ this fails. In the down-set model, compl(α(x)) is an up-set, not a down-set. So either Σ has extra structure (e.g. closed under complement, or c_{E'} is a duality/pseudo-complement inside Σ_{E'}), or the condition 'R(x) ∈ Σ_{E'}' should read with respect to a dual family. This cannot be decided from this page alone.
The bijectivity of ψ is asserted but not proved on this page or the next. Only the φ bijection is proved on p. 95.

ideas.what: Morphisms of 'dispositions' as maps Σ_E → Σ_{E'} commuting with arbitrary sups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical lattice theory; Joyal–Tierney 1984 for Sup as a monoidal category

ideas.what: Equivalence: sup-maps on a sup-generated lattice ↔ suitably monotone maps on generators E → Σ_{E'}
ideas.modern_name: Free sup-lattice / down-set completion universal property (Kan extension along Yoneda for 2-enriched categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (enriched category theory; Lawvere 1973 for 2-enriched view)

ideas.what: Equivalence with relations R ⊂ E×E' whose fibres on both sides are distinguished subsets (via complementation)
ideas.modern_name: Monotone relations / 2-valued profunctors (distributors); Galois-type duality between relations and sup-maps

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard verification that sup-preserving maps between lattices of distinguished subsets correspond to generator-level maps and to two-sided-fibred relations, i.e. sup-lattice morphisms and 2-valued profunctors. It belongs to Grothendieck's private 1986 'dispositions' project, but the content is well known.
transcription_corrections: 'composant avec c_{Σ'}' — the image shows 'c_{Σ'}' in the text and 'c_{E'}' over the arrow. The target appears to be 'Σ_{E'} ⊂ P(E')' with P struck and overwritten, consistent with the transcription.
'α(x) |0| x'' likely denotes a disjointness/non-incidence relation between α(x) and x' (explained as x' ∈ compl_{E'}(α(x))).
